title: Oyster Po’ Boy (Cornmeal-Fried Oysters)
summary: Shucked oysters dipped in egg, tossed in seasoned cornmeal and flour and fried at 190 °C for 2-3 minutes. Piled into toasted French bread dressed with mayonnaise, lettuce, tomato and pickles.

ingredients.item: freshly shucked oysters, well drained and kept cold
fine sea salt or table salt, to finish
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
sections of soft French bread or po’ boy rolls, about 20 cm long, split and lightly toasted

steps.title: Coat the oysters
steps.text: Drain the oysters well; excess liquid stops the coating sticking. Beat the eggs in one bowl and mix the cornmeal, flour and Creole seasoning in another. Dip six oysters at a time in egg, let the excess drip off, then toss them in the coating.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat oil 5 cm deep to 190 °C and fry in batches for 2-3 min, stirring gently, until golden and crisp and the bubbling slows. Drain on the paper-lined rack and sprinkle with the pinch of salt.

steps.title: Dress the bread
steps.text: Spread the toasted bread with mayonnaise, lay tomato and pickles on the top halves and shredded lettuce on the bottoms.

steps.title: Pile and serve
steps.text: Pile six oysters into each sandwich, press together and eat at once with lemon wedges.

tips: Keep the oysters very cold until frying so they stay plump.
Very hot oil cooks the coating fast, before the oysters overcook.
Large prawns can replace the oysters for a shrimp po' boy.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Eat immediately; fried oysters do not keep well. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
